content:
Apple and the EU's long-running antitrust dispute over iPhone app sales appears to have finally been resolved.

The EU has welcomed Apple's new app commission fees in the region. Under the revised terms, developers will pay commissions or fees ranging from 5% to 26%, depending on their revenue and chosen sales channels…

EU law requires Apple to allow third-party app stores to operate. While Apple has complied, it has faced complaints over the commissions and fees it charges for third-party sales.

Apple rolled out the new terms fully this week, and the EU appears to be satisfied.

  • For App Store apps transacting through Apple's In-App Purchase feature, the commission will be 26%. For the vast majority of developers — including those participating in the App Store Small Business Programme, the Mini Apps Partner Programme, or the Video Partner Programme, as well as auto-renewing subscriptions after the first year — the commission will be 15%.
  • For App Store apps that use alternative payment processing, the commission will be 20%. Developers in the aforementioned programmes will enjoy a lower rate of 10%.
  • For App Store apps that direct users via a link to complete purchases outside the app, the commission will be 15%. Developers in the aforementioned programmes will enjoy a lower rate of 10%.
  • For apps distributed through alternative app marketplaces or the web, Apple will charge a 5% Core Technology Commission.

The European Commission told the Irish Independent it welcomes Apple's new terms.

"The Commission welcomes Apple's adjustments to its commercial terms. These adjustments stem from the close dialogue between the Commission and Apple following the non-compliance decision issued in April regarding Apple's steering terms and the preliminary findings on alternative app distribution," a spokesperson said. "With the new arrangements announced today, the Commission will closely monitor Apple's effective implementation of the new terms."

9to5Mac's Take

This protracted legal battle now appears to be resolved. However, the situation in the United States tells a different story. In the latest development, Apple is seeking to open settlement talks with Epic Games, but the game developer believes such talks would be unproductive. The court will decide on the next steps.
